knowledgePath: Domain Model > Practical > Picking Entity Type
question: You're modeling a temporary filter UI state that should not survive page reload. Which entity type fits?
explanation: NPEs live in memory only — exactly right for transient state. Persistable would needlessly write to the database; External is for remote data; View is for read-only OQL results.

question: You need to store product prices that may reach 9999.99 EUR. Which attribute type?
explanation: Decimal is purpose-built for high-precision money. Float doesn't exist in Mendix. Integer would force you to store cents and convert. String loses arithmetic ability.

question: Each Article can have several Tags. Which multiplicity do you choose?
explanation: Many-to-many: each Article has many Tags AND each Tag can apply to many Articles. 1-to-* would mean each Tag belongs to ONE Article — wrong. 1-to-1 limits to one Tag per Article.

question: You want to record WHO last changed an Order. The simplest approach is:
explanation: System Member changedBy automatically references the System.User who committed the change — zero custom code. Manual attributes, separate audit entities, or Java actions are all more work for the same outcome.

question: You have Employee and Manager. Both share Name, Email, Department but Manager also has DirectReports. Best modeling approach?
options: Two unrelated entities with copies of shared fields
One Person entity with a 'role' enum
explanation: Manager is a more specific Employee — generalization Employee → specialization Manager. Inverting the inheritance would be wrong (Employee would inherit DirectReports). Copying fields breaks DRY; using an enum is fine for simple cases but loses type-safety for Manager-specific behavior.

question: You need to log diagnostic information to the server log from a microflow. Which activity?
explanation: Log Message writes to the server log — exactly the requirement. Show Message produces a popup for the END USER. Email is unrelated. Java is overkill for a built-in operation.

question: You need to iterate over every Order in a list and mark it as Archived. Which loop type?
options: No loop needed — use Change List
explanation: For Each over the Order list is the natural choice. While is for condition-based iteration. Recursion adds complexity. Change List adds or removes objects from a list but doesn't modify their attributes.

question: Your microflow uses Change Object to set Customer.Status = 'Active'. Without further action, will this persist after the microflow ends?
options: No — you must call Commit to persist
Only if security is set to Production
explanation: Change Object modifies in memory only. Without Commit, the change is lost when the session ends. This is THE most common Mendix beginner trap: forgetting the Commit step.

question: After a successful Order creation in a microflow, you want to navigate the user to the OrderDetail page. Which activity?
explanation: Show Page sends the user to a specified page, passing the relevant object as parameter. Show Message displays text only; Open URL is for external URLs; Set Variable doesn't navigate.

question: You're creating a microflow that calculates the total price of an Order — called only by other microflows. Recommended naming prefix?
explanation: SUB_ marks reusable internal microflows called by others. CAL_ is specifically for calculated-attribute microflows (not the case here). ACT_ is for page actions. DS_ is for data source microflows on pages.

question: You want to validate that an email field contains '@' before the form submits — without a server round-trip. Where do you implement this?
explanation: Nanoflows run client-side — instant validation without server hit. Microflow validation works but is slower (network round-trip). Java is server-only and overkill. Database triggers aren't a Mendix concept.

question: An offline mobile field-worker app needs to push local changes to the server when WiFi is available. Which activity?
explanation: Synchronize is purpose-built for offline-online data exchange. Individual Commits would each need network access (failing offline). REST is server-side only. Show Message is UI feedback, not data sync.

question: In an online app, you compute the total of three input fields and display it instantly. Where do you implement this?
options: A nanoflow triggered by on-change on each field
explanation: Pure UI math = nanoflow. No database = no network hit. Microflow + button is clunky UX. Scheduled events are time-triggered, not user-triggered. External JS bypasses Mendix needlessly.

question: You're debugging a nanoflow and add a Log Message activity. Where does the output appear?
explanation: Nanoflow Log Message → browser console. For server logs you'd use a microflow's Log Message activity. People looking in the wrong place is a top debugging time-sink.

question: You need to access the device's GPS coordinates inside a flow. Where do you implement this?
options: A microflow with a REST call to a geolocation service
A nanoflow with a JavaScript action calling navigator.geolocation
explanation: Device APIs (camera, GPS, localStorage) are client-side — only nanoflows reach them, via JavaScript actions. Microflows can't access browser/device APIs. Java is server-side. XPath is a query language.

question: You're building a payment-processing module you plan to sell on the Mendix Marketplace. Which module type?
explanation: Add-on modules are designed for Marketplace distribution: reusable, protected. App modules are for primary app development. Solution modules are for packaged ISV solutions. System is built-in only.

question: A teammate needs to inspect and modify the module's microflows you built. Which export format?
options: No export needed, share via screenshare
explanation: .mpk includes full editable source — perfect for team sharing. .mxmodule is protected/read-only for Marketplace distribution. Screensharing isn't a sharing format; it doesn't transfer the code.

question: In your Reporting module you want to use the Customer entity defined in the Sales module. What's needed?
options: Copy the Customer entity into Reporting
Add Sales as a dependency of Reporting
Use a REST call between the two modules
explanation: Dependencies tab on Reporting adds Sales as a dependency. Then Sales.Customer is accessible (assuming the entity's Export Level allows it). Copying creates two diverging entities. REST between same-app modules is overkill.

question: A Marketplace module you installed asks you to place a third-party JAR in your project. Where does it go?
explanation: External JARs go in the project-level userlib/ folder. actions/ is for your Java code; proxies/ is auto-generated and shouldn't be touched. docs/ isn't a build folder.

question: You want only Manager users in your app to see the Sales module's pages. Where do you configure this?
options: Module Security: define a Module Role with the right page access, then link it to the Manager User Role in App Security
explanation: Page access lives in Module Security via Module Roles. App Security composes those Module Roles into User Roles like Manager. Per-page settings exist but they're configured under module security, not directly on each page.

question: You're deploying to Mendix Cloud's licensed production environment. Which app security level is required?
explanation: Production is required for licensed Mendix Cloud. Off is for local/Free Apps only. Prototype/Demo applies auth but no entity rules — unsafe for real users. 'Maintenance' isn't a security level.

question: You want unauthenticated users to be able to browse the public catalog but not submit orders. What do you configure?
options: Enable anonymous access and assign the single allowed user role with read-only catalog rights
Use a custom microflow to filter
explanation: Anonymous = ONE user role with whatever rights you want them to have. Read-only on the catalog entity, no access on Order — exactly the pattern. Disabling anonymous would block browsing. Global read-only would block legit users from submitting orders.

question: Calculated attribute TotalScore on Customer should be visible to admins but hidden from regular users. How?
options: Set the access rule for Customer.TotalScore: Read for Admin, no access for Regular
Use a microflow to conditionally compute
Hide the attribute in the page only
explanation: Access rules on calculated attributes work normally for Read — granting per role. Changing to stored is unnecessary. Conditional microflow logic is more work than declarative access. Page-level hiding is UX, not security (deeplinks bypass it).

question: You want users to see only their own Orders. Which XPath constraint on the access rule?
explanation: `[%CurrentUser%]` is the XPath token resolving to the System.User object. Note the brackets and percentages — strict syntax. Variables ($) and literal strings don't work as runtime user references in XPath constraints.

question: You want to restrict who can execute the ACT_DeleteOrder microflow. Where do you configure this?
options: Inside the microflow's first activity (an If check)
On the page button calling it
explanation: Microflow execution access lives in Module Security under Microflow access. App Security composes module roles into user roles but doesn't directly grant microflow access. In-microflow checks duplicate the framework; button-level checks are UX-only.

question: You want a table showing all Customers, with paging and column sorting. Which widget?
explanation: Data Grid shows multiple objects with paging and column sort built-in. Data View is for one object. Reference Selector is for selecting an associated object. List View is for custom-rendered list items (no built-in paging UI like a grid).

knowledgePath: Pages > Practical > Reference Selector vs Set
question: On an Order edit form, the user needs to pick ONE Customer. Which widget?
explanation: Reference Selector = pick ONE associated object (1-to-many association). Reference Set Selector handles MULTIPLE selections (many-to-many). Data Grid is overkill. Enum dropdowns are for enumerations, not entity references.

question: A data view should display the Order that was passed from the previous page as a parameter. Which data source?
explanation: Context = 'use the object already provided to the page'. Microflow would re-fetch unnecessarily. Database is a grid source, not a data view source. Listen to widget is for selection-driven detail panes.

question: You're building a 'Customer summary card' that should appear identically on multiple pages. Which mechanism?
options: Copy-paste the widget group on every page
Create a Snippet and embed it
explanation: Snippets are exactly for reusable widget groups. Layouts wrap pages (shared chrome). Page Templates are starting points for new pages. Copy-paste is the anti-pattern — changes require N edits.

question: On an Order detail page, an admin can edit; a regular user can only view. Best way?
options: Two separate pages and conditional navigation
Editability = Conditionally with expression based on current user role
Hide the data view from regular users
explanation: Conditional Editability with an expression checking `$currentUser` role is declarative and clean. Two pages doubles maintenance. Hiding the data view leaves regulars with no view. Disabling Save manually is a half-measure.

question: You need to retrieve Customers with the surname 'Jansen' inside a Studio Pro microflow XPath constraint. What do you write?
explanation: Inside Studio Pro the entity is implicit — write only the bracketed constraint. Full //Sales.Customer[...] is for Java/service code. Dot notation and SQL are wrong dialects.

question: Find Orders where IsPaid is true.
explanation: Boolean literals in XPath are functions: `true()` and `false()`. The bare keyword and string/integer comparisons are wrong.

question: Find Customers without an Email value.
explanation: `= empty` is Mendix XPath's null/missing check. `= null` is SQL; empty-string `''` only matches truly empty strings (not null); 'is not set' isn't valid XPath.

question: Find Orders created in the last 7 days using XPath, where $sevenDaysAgo is a DateTime variable.
explanation: Compare directly with the typed variable. Mendix XPath uses standard comparison operators on dates. Special keywords like WITHIN or 'last7days' don't exist.

question: Find Orders that are Paid AND have Total > 100.
explanation: XPath uses lowercase `and`. Uppercase AND and `&&` are wrong dialects. Comma-separation isn't AND in XPath.

question: Your app needs to fetch weather data from a public REST API. Which activity in a microflow?
explanation: Call REST Service is the activity for REST APIs. Call Web Service is SOAP. Show Page doesn't fetch data. Import with mapping converts already-fetched data.

question: You receive JSON from a partner API and need to populate Mendix Customer entities. What artifact?
explanation: Import Mapping converts incoming JSON/XML into Mendix objects. Export Mapping goes the other way (Mendix → JSON/XML). Java is overkill. Constants are configuration values.

question: You want to expose your Customer data as a REST endpoint other apps can call. Steps?
options: Right-click entity > Expose as REST resource, then configure authentication
explanation: Right-click on the entity > Expose as REST resource is the built-in path. No Apache, servlets, or required Marketplace modules. Authentication is configured in the published service settings.

question: Importing Customer data daily from a partner — you don't want to create duplicates if they already exist. Which Import Mapping option?
options: Find by key (using Email as key)
explanation: Find by key matches incoming rows against existing objects by the chosen key (Email) — update if found, create otherwise. Create object always inserts (duplicates). Skip isn't an option. Custom logic works but reinvents the built-in pattern.

question: A Call REST Service activity fails. To inspect the HTTP status code and response body in the error handler, you use:
explanation: $latestHttpResponse holds the REST-specific response details. $latestError is the generic error variable (message, type, stacktrace). $lastError and $response don't exist.

question: Your microflow needs to call a complex string-encryption algorithm not available in Mendix. Best approach?
options: Implement the encryption inside a Java action and call it from the microflow
Write the algorithm as a nanoflow
Build it from microflow String activities
explanation: Java actions extend microflow capability when modeler-level activities don't cover your need. Nanoflows are client-side (unsafe for encryption keys). String activities can't implement encryption from scratch. Avoiding encryption isn't an option for sensitive data.

question: You add a new line of Java code to a generated action class. Where do you put it so it survives the next 'Deploy for Eclipse'?
options: Between the //BEGIN USER CODE and //END USER CODE markers
explanation: Only code inside the USER CODE markers is preserved across regenerations. Outside them, code is overwritten. Comments aren't preserved either. proxies/ is auto-generated and should never be hand-edited.

question: Your Java action needs to use Apache POI for Excel parsing. Where does the JAR go?
explanation: External JARs go in userlib/. Studio Pro picks them up at build time. actions/ is for your Java code; proxies/ is auto-generated; node_modules/ is for JavaScript packages, not JARs.

question: How do you add a Java action call to a microflow?
options: Type `call MyJavaAction()` in a Decision expression
Drag the Java action from App Explorer onto the microflow as an activity
Java actions can only be called from other Java
explanation: Drag the Java action into the microflow — same as a sub-microflow. Decisions use expressions, not method calls. Call Web Service is for SOAP. Java actions are absolutely callable from microflows (that's their whole purpose).

question: You need a client-side action with custom code. Which type do you create?
explanation: JavaScript actions are the client-side counterpart of Java actions — used from nanoflows. Java actions are server-side only. A microflow runs server-side. Nanoflows host JS actions but aren't themselves 'custom code'.

question: You want every new Order to automatically get OrderNumber = current count + 1 when created. Which event handler?
options: Before Create event handler — generate the number before commit
explanation: After Create receives the new object and can modify it before commit. Before Create runs BEFORE the object exists (no parameter). After Commit is too late (already saved). Validation rules check, don't generate.

question: You want to prevent committing an Order with Total = 0. Which mechanism stops the commit?
options: After Commit handler that rolls back
A validation rule of type Range
explanation: A Range validation rule on Total > 0 enforces this declaratively. A Before Commit returning false also works but is more code. After Commit can't prevent (commit already happened). Assertions aren't a Mendix-native concept.

question: Customer.Email must never be empty. Quickest enforcement?
options: Required validation rule on the Email attribute
explanation: Required validation rule is one-click and declarative. Before Commit works but is more setup. Microflow checks at every save means modifying every save flow. JS validation is client-side and bypassed by direct DB writes.

question: Two customers shouldn't be able to use the same Email. Built-in enforcement?
options: Manual XPath check in Before Commit
explanation: Unique validation rule. Mendix handles the underlying database index and uniqueness check. Manual XPath in Before Commit is what Unique does for you. DB constraints exist but you don't write them in Mendix. Frontend checks alone are bypassable.

question: You write a microflow that runs before an Order is committed. Recommended name?
explanation: BCO_ = Before Commit (B + CO). The entity name follows the prefix. ACT_ is for page actions. Generic names like ValidateOrder lose role information. SUB_ is for general sub-microflows.

question: An Order has statuses: Open, Processing, Closed. Best attribute type?
explanation: Enumerations are purpose-built for fixed value sets. Strings allow typos. Integer codes lose readability. Boolean can't represent 3 states. Enumerations also support translation via captions.

question: You want OrderStatus 'Open' to appear in Dutch as 'Open' and in English as 'Open' too. Where do you set this?
options: Edit the Name to be localized
Translate the Caption per language via the Language Menu
explanation: Captions are translatable per language; the Name stays as one technical identifier. Editing Names would invalidate stored data. Per-language enums duplicate the model. Translation isn't automatic — you do it through the Language Menu.

question: You have a partner API whose URL is 'https://api-prod.partner.com' in production and 'https://api-test.partner.com' in test. Best storage?
options: Hardcode in the Call REST Service activity
A microflow that picks based on conditions
explanation: Constants support per-environment overrides — set 'PartnerApiUrl' default to one and override in cloud env config. Hardcoding means rebuilding for prod vs test. Microflow branching is unnecessary. Entity attributes are for runtime data, not config.

question: You add a constant 'NewSearchEnabled' (Boolean) that nanoflows on the search page check. Required property?
explanation: Exposed to Client = Yes ships the value to nanoflows and page expressions. Without it, nanoflows can't read the constant. Documentation, default value, and export level are independent choices but Exposed to Client is the gating requirement.

question: You compare $order/Status to the Open enum value in a Decision. Recommended form?
explanation: Typed reference is build-time safe — rename or remove 'Open' and the Decision fails to compile. String forms only fail at runtime, and getCaption is locale-dependent.

question: You want to delete old log entries every night at 2:00 AM UTC. What do you create?
options: A scheduled event with Daily interval at 2:00 UTC
explanation: Scheduled events are exactly for time-based automatic execution. After Commit handlers fire on commits, not on a schedule. Nanoflows need a user trigger. REST endpoints need to be called.

question: During maintenance you want to stop a scheduled event for a week without deleting it. Action?
options: Toggle the Enabled property to false
Delete and remember to recreate later
explanation: Enabled toggle suspends execution cleanly. Renaming doesn't disable. Weird intervals are hacky. Deleting risks forgetting to recreate.

question: A scheduled event runs a microflow that cleans up old ProcessedQueueTask rows. Recommended microflow name?
explanation: There's no formal SE_ prefix in core docs but many teams use it for scheduled events for clarity. ACT_ is for page actions and DS_ for data sources — those would mislead readers. Naming for clarity is the point.

question: You deploy your app as a Free App on Mendix Cloud. What happens to scheduled events?
options: They run but only once per day max
They don't run at all in Free Apps
explanation: Free Apps explicitly don't execute scheduled events. To run them in production you need licensed Mendix Cloud or another paid tier. Test locally to verify scheduled events work correctly.

question: Your daily report runs at 09:00 'server time'. Mendix Cloud runs on UTC. A user in Amsterdam expects it at their 09:00. What do you do?
options: Set the schedule to 07:00 UTC so Amsterdam users see it at 09:00 (winter) — but accept DST drift
explanation: Mendix Cloud is UTC; Amsterdam is UTC+1 (winter) or UTC+2 (summer). Choose UTC-anchored schedules that approximate the local time you want, accepting DST shifts — or implement per-user fan-out at hourly granularity for true per-user delivery.

question: A new feature request comes in mid-sprint. Where does it go?
options: Add to the current sprint immediately
Add to the Product Backlog for the PO to prioritize for a future sprint
explanation: Mid-sprint scope changes break the sprint commitment. The PO triages backlog items for upcoming sprints. Rejecting all new ideas is unagile. Implementing without prioritization is chaos.

question: At your daily standup, what should you typically share?
options: A full demo of your work
What you did yesterday, what you'll do today, any blockers
explanation: The classic 3-part standup: progress, plan, blockers. Demos belong at sprint review. Slack messages and timesheets aren't standup content.

question: You're writing a story for a 'login button' feature. Best phrasing?
options: As a registered user, I want to sign in with email and password so that I can access my dashboard
explanation: Stories follow 'As [role], I want [goal], so that [reason]'. Implementation details ('login button', 'JWT') belong in tasks underneath. The story format keeps user value central.

question: Three story points means…
options: A relative size compared to other stories (e.g. slightly bigger than a 2-pointer)
explanation: Story points are RELATIVE — a 3 is bigger than a 2 and smaller than a 5. They factor complexity + effort + uncertainty. Absolute time mappings vary by team and person.

question: Two developers branch from main: one works on the Sales module, the other on the Orders module. When both merge back, what's expected?
options: Always conflicts because Mendix is monolithic
Clean auto-merge because the changes are in different modules
Only one merge is allowed at a time
explanation: Mendix Team Server (Git underneath) auto-merges non-overlapping changes — different modules, different microflows. Conflicts only arise when both edit the same document. Branching is the standard parallel-work pattern.

question: You need to model both Persons and Companies as customers in a CRM. Most flexible approach?
options: Two unrelated entities Person and Company
Abstract Customer with specializations Person and Company
One entity with a 'type' enum and nullable fields per type
Reuse the same Customer entity for both
explanation: Generalization Customer → Person, Company gives shared attributes (Email, Address) plus type-specific ones (DateOfBirth for Person, VATNumber for Company). Single entity with nullable fields creates data integrity gaps. Unrelated entities duplicate shared logic.

question: When deleting a Project, all associated Tasks should be removed too. When deleting a Task, the Project should remain. Which delete behaviors?
options: Project → Task: cascade delete; Task → Project: keep
Project → Task: keep; Task → Project: cascade
explanation: Cascade from Project to Task removes tasks when project is deleted. From Task to Project = keep, so deleting a task leaves the project intact. Delete behavior is set PER side of the association.

knowledgePath: Domain Model > Practical > Calculated vs Stored
question: An Order has many OrderLines. You need Order.Total. The Total is shown on a list of 1000 Orders. Best approach for performance?
options: Calculated attribute that sums OrderLines on every retrieve
Stored attribute updated by an After Commit handler on OrderLine
Compute on the page via expression
Use a microflow data source on the grid
explanation: Stored is much faster for list views (no per-row microflow). Update it via OrderLine commit handlers to keep it in sync. Calculated would mean 1000 microflow executions per page load. Page expressions can't sum lists. Microflow data source still has to compute somehow.

knowledgePath: Domain Model > Practical > NPE in Microflow
question: You want to gather user filter selections (date range, status) before retrieving Orders. Best modeling?
options: A persistable FilterState entity per user
A non-persistable FilterState entity created in the microflow
Pass each filter value as a separate microflow parameter
explanation: NPE bundles filter values into one object — clean parameter passing, no DB write, no cleanup needed. Persistable creates orphan rows. Many parameters get unwieldy. Page params alone work for simple cases but NPE scales better.

question: In a hospital app, Patient has up to 5 attending Doctors and a Doctor has many Patients. The association owner should be:
options: Patient — fewer Doctors to track per Patient
Doctor — they are higher in the hierarchy
explanation: Many-to-many between Patient and Doctor with owner Default stores the association on Patient (the side you draw from). The modeler's recommendation: 'start from the side with more instances' — there are usually more patients than doctors per day.

question: You need to update 5000 Customers, setting LoyaltyTier based on TotalSpent. Best approach?
options: For Each loop with Change Object + Commit per iteration
For Each loop with Change Object, then a single Commit Object(s) on the full list at the end
explanation: Batching to a single Commit at the end is dramatically faster than 5000 commits — one transaction vs 5000. Recursion offers no perf benefit. A scheduled event might run the work but the same batching applies.

question: Your microflow imports CSV data row by row. If row 50 fails, you want rows 1-49 to be saved and the failure logged. Which error handling on the import sub-microflow call?
options: Custom without rollback — preserves rows 1-49 before the failure
explanation: Custom without rollback preserves changes made before the failure — exactly the requirement. Default rollback wipes all 49 successes. Custom with rollback also reverts. Continue silently swallows, making debugging harder.

question: You have a list of Orders. You need the ones with Total > 100 AND from this month. Most idiomatic?
options: For Each loop, push to a new list per match
List Operation: Filter with both conditions in the expression
explanation: Filter with a combined boolean expression is one step, readable, fast. If the list comes from the database, XPath at retrieve time is even better. Loops are imperative noise. Two filters is just one filter split.

question: You have a list of Vehicles. Cars need fuel cost calculations; Trucks need cargo-weight calculations. Inside a For Each loop, how do you branch?
options: Object Type Decision with paths for Car and Truck
explanation: Object Type Decision branches on the specialization automatically AND gives you a typed reference per branch (no manual Cast). Attribute-based decisions need a Cast follow-up. Casting unconditionally is wasteful. Two microflows would re-iterate the list.

question: From a button on a page, ACT_PlaceOrder calls SUB_ValidateInventory. The user lacks access to SUB_ValidateInventory but has access to ACT_PlaceOrder. What happens?
options: The call to SUB_ fails with a permission error
Both run — internal microflow calls aren't re-checked for role
The button is hidden at deploy time
explanation: Role checks apply only to client-initiated invocations. Once a microflow is running, internal calls bypass role checks. This is intentional — but it means microflow access alone isn't a security boundary.

question: You build a nanoflow that, on page load, retrieves the user's Orders from the database. The page feels slow. Why?
options: Retrieving persistable entities in an online nanoflow triggers a network round-trip — same cost as a microflow plus extra overhead
Mendix prevents nanoflows from accessing the database in browsers
explanation: Online nanoflows that touch persistable entities phone home for every Create/Retrieve/Commit. The 'fast because client-side' advantage only applies when there's no database work. For Order retrieval, use a microflow data source on the page; reserve nanoflows for pure UI logic.

question: Your JavaScript action calls fetch() and returns a Promise that resolves in 2 seconds. The nanoflow then calls Show Message with the result. What does the user see during those 2 seconds?
options: The page remains responsive; Show Message appears after the Promise resolves
Nothing — Show Message runs immediately with empty data
explanation: JavaScript actions are async-aware. The nanoflow waits for the Promise without blocking the UI. Show Message fires once the result is ready. Treating JS actions as synchronous is a common misconception.

question: You want to build a nanoflow that creates many NPE objects without server round-trips for filtering UI state. What must you avoid on the NPE?
options: Event handlers, calculated attributes, and read-only attributes
explanation: NPE Create stays client-side ONLY if the NPE has no event handlers, calculated attributes, or read-only attributes. Adding any of these forces the runtime to involve the server. Other features (validation rules don't apply to NPEs; required is fine; generalization is fine) don't trigger this.

question: Your offline mobile app has 50,000 Customer rows on the server. The first Synchronize call downloads ALL of them, making startup slow. Best fix?
options: Live with it — first sync is always slow
Add offline access rules with XPath constraints so each user syncs only their own subset
Run sync in the background after login
explanation: Offline access rules with XPath narrow what each user syncs (e.g. their assigned customers only). 50K → maybe 100 customers per user = fast. Compression doesn't reduce row count; background sync still pulls 50K. Constrain the data.

question: A nanoflow on page A opens page B via Show Page, passing $Order. After Show Page, the nanoflow does Commit Object on $Order. Will page B see the committed change?
options: No — Show Page captures a snapshot
Yes — objects pass by reference; page B holds the same object reference and sees the update
Only if page B refreshes manually
Depends on the data source of page B's data view
explanation: Mendix passes objects by reference. Subsequent mutations to $Order are visible on page B because both screens share the same in-memory object. The data source choice affects initial load behavior but not subsequent reference-based updates.

question: A Marketplace add-on module exposes Customer entity at Usable level. You need a CustomerExtended with extra fields. Approach?
options: Create a specialization CustomerExtended in your own module that extends the add-on's Customer
explanation: Specialization works because Usable allows reference and inheritance. Editing the add-on is impossible (.mxmodule is protected) and breaks updates. Forking diverges you from upstream. Re-implementing loses the add-on's functionality.

question: You install Marketplace module A using guava 30.x. Now you install module B that requires guava 32.x. What's expected?
options: Studio Pro keeps the newer version; you must verify A still works with 32.x
explanation: Studio Pro deduplicates JARs to the newer version. The Mendix runtime has ONE classpath — so A's code runs against guava 32 even though it was built against 30. If A relies on 30-only methods, you get runtime errors. Always test after JAR upgrades.

question: You want to share a module with another team within your org, source-included, so they can adapt it. Export format?
explanation: .mpk = full source for internal sharing. .mxmodule is protected/read-only (for Marketplace where you don't want consumers reading source). .zip and screenshots aren't valid module export formats.

question: Your add-on module is at version 1.2.0. You add a breaking change (renaming an entity). New version should be?
explanation: Semantic versioning: breaking changes bump the major (2.0.0). Minor adds backward-compatible features (1.3.0). Patch fixes bugs (1.2.1). Renaming an entity breaks references in consuming apps — explicitly major.

question: Module Sales has access rules on Customer. You import a new module Reporting that needs to query Customer. What works?
options: Reporting must declare module roles compatible with Sales's, then link them at app level
Reporting cannot query Customer at all
explanation: Each module declares its own roles. App Security composes them into User Roles. Access rules respect the composed user role's combined module rights. Reporting can't auto-inherit (that'd bypass the composition pattern).

question: Access rule XPath: `[Project/Sales.Project_Member/Sales.Member[Member_User='[%CurrentUser%]']]`. The table has 5M rows. Performance is poor. First fix?
options: Restructure data so the User reference lives directly on the entity, eliminating the 3-hop join
explanation: Each '/' in XPath is a JOIN. 3-hop joins on millions of rows are expensive. Restructuring to a single direct reference dramatically reduces query cost. Disabling security is dangerous; microflow pre-filtering breaks security guarantees; page size doesn't help indexed/joined queries.

knowledgePath: Security > Practical > Run With All Rights
question: In an Order workflow, you want a normal User to trigger a microflow that internally needs to create an Audit row. The User has no Create access on Audit. What enables this?
options: Add Create access to User for Audit
Set 'Run with all rights' on the microflow that creates the Audit
explanation: 'Run with all rights' on a sub-microflow lets it perform DB operations the calling user can't — useful for system-level invariants. Grant the user Create on Audit and you'd allow them to create arbitrary audit rows. Java actions also have an elevated context but a microflow setting is simpler.

knowledgePath: Security > Practical > Page vs Entity Security
question: You hide page 'AdminPanel' from regular users via Module Security. A regular user crafts a deeplink URL to it. What protects the data?
options: Only the entity access rules on the data displayed by the page
explanation: Page hide only removes from navigation menus — deeplinks bypass it. Real data protection requires entity-level access rules. The pattern is BOTH: page hide for UX + entity rules for security.

question: You want public visitors to browse the product catalog without signing in, AND signed-in users to see prices. How?
options: Enable Anonymous access with read-only role; restrict price visibility to signed-in roles via entity access rules
explanation: Anonymous user gets the public catalog access (one role). Signed-in users get additional role granting price visibility. Entity access rules per role decide who sees what attributes. Two apps duplicates everything; forcing sign-in blocks public browsing.

question: An access rule on Project: Create=true with XPath `[Owner = '[%CurrentUser%]']`. Customer A tries to create a Project setting Owner=Customer B. What happens?
options: Allowed — XPath constraints don't apply to Create operations
explanation: XPath constraints filter Read/Write/Delete on EXISTING rows but don't apply to Create. To enforce 'Owner must be current user' on creation, use a Before Create event handler that sets Owner explicitly. This rule trips up many access-control designers.

question: You have a grid showing Orders with search and column-sort. You want fast filtering on millions of rows. Best data source?
options: Database — search and sort pushed to SQL
explanation: Database source pushes search/sort to the database, fast and indexed. Microflow source returns a fully-materialized list; search/sort happens in-memory in the runtime, slow on millions. Association is for related-object lists, not free-form queries.

question: You have a tabbed Order Edit page with a nested data view showing CustomerProfile inside one tab. You want save/cancel buttons in that nested view. Where do they go?
options: Inside the nested data view's body (e.g. a container at the bottom)
explanation: Nested data view footers are ALWAYS invisible — you can't make them appear. Place buttons in the body as a regular container. The outer footer works but interferes with the overall page save/cancel.

question: On a Customer detail page, only admins should be able to edit. Best UI pattern?
options: Two separate pages, navigate based on role
Data view Editability = Conditionally with expression based on $currentUser/role
Use App Security to block the page
explanation: Conditional Editability with expression `member of role 'Admin'` is declarative and centralized. Two pages doubles maintenance. Hiding save only is incomplete (form still appears editable). Blocking the page entirely prevents view-only access.

question: You build a snippet 'OrderSummary' that requires an Order parameter. You want to embed it on a page whose context is Customer. How?
options: Wrap the snippet in a data view that retrieves the Order from Customer via a microflow source
Change the snippet to take Customer
Add a button that opens a popup with the snippet
explanation: Snippet parameters must be supplied. Wrapping in a data view sourced from a microflow that returns Customer→Order satisfies the parameter without changing the snippet. Changing the snippet's signature defeats reuse. Auto context reading isn't supported for snippets.

question: You're migrating a classic web app to native mobile and React. Your pages use classic Data Grid. Replacement?
options: Data Grid 2 — designed for React client and offers similar functionality
Don't migrate — use a compatibility shim
explanation: Data Grid 2 is the React-client replacement with comparable features plus virtualization. Gallery is a card-style layout, not a grid. List View has different rendering. Compatibility shims for classic Data Grid don't exist.

question: You filter Customers by `[contains(Name, 'jansen')]` and the query is slow on millions of rows. Why?
options: contains() translates to SQL LIKE '%jansen%' which cannot use an index — full table scan
Strings shorter than 8 chars can't be matched
explanation: LIKE '%pattern%' bypasses btree indexes. Alternatives: index-friendly startsWith(), or full-text search via database extensions. Mendix does support contains() — it's just expensive at scale.

question: You want Orders whose Customer's Name starts with 'A'. The association is Sales.Customer_Order between Order and Customer. XPath?
explanation: XPath navigates via association name + target entity. startsWith() is the right function for prefix matching. Dot notation isn't valid XPath. SQL syntax doesn't apply.

question: In an access rule on Project, you want projects whose Manager equals the current user. Constraint?
explanation: Navigate via the association name to the System.User and compare with the `[%CurrentUser%]` token. `$currentUser` is for microflow expressions, not XPath constraints. `currentUser()` and `[%User%]` aren't real tokens.

question: Find Orders that have NO associated Invoice (Sales.Order_Invoice association exists).
explanation: `= empty` and `not(association/target)` are both valid ways to check for absence. `= null` is SQL. Knowing both forms is useful — different patterns read more naturally in different contexts.

question: XPath `[Name = 'jansen']` finds nothing, even though 'Jansen' exists. What's happening?
options: Both A and B describe the issue. Fix: `[toLowerCase(Name) = 'jansen']` or use contains()
Mendix encodes Names as UTF-16, breaking comparison
explanation: XPath string equality is case-sensitive. Fix by normalizing both sides with toLowerCase() or using contains() (still case-sensitive by default, but you can pair with toLowerCase). UTF-16 encoding is not the issue.

question: You consume a partner REST API that returns 100 records per page with `?page=N` parameter and a `next_page` field. Your microflow needs ALL results. Approach?
options: Call once with page=1 and assume that's all
Loop: call REST, accumulate, while next_page is non-empty, increment page; recurrence terminates when next_page is empty
explanation: Standard pagination = loop until exhausted. Accumulate results into a list. `next_page` empty ends the loop. There's no ?page=ALL convention. Recursion works but offers no advantage over a loop and risks stack overflow on many pages.

question: A REST call to a slow partner takes up to 120 seconds. You hit a 30-second timeout. Fix?
options: Configure the timeout property on the Call REST Service activity to allow 120s+
explanation: Call REST has configurable timeouts. Default may be conservative; raising it for legitimately-slow services is the fix. Retrying without raising the timeout would still timeout. SOAP has timeouts too. Nanoflows can't call REST directly.

question: You call a payment-create REST endpoint. The network drops mid-request — you didn't get a response. Your error handler retries. Risk?
options: The retry safely overwrites the original
If the original actually succeeded, the retry creates a second payment — a double-charge
REST calls are idempotent by definition
explanation: Dropped response doesn't mean dropped request — the server may have processed it. Naive retries create duplicates. Mitigation: use an Idempotency-Key header (if API supports), or query before retry. This is a top distributed-systems pitfall, not a Mendix one — but it bites you in Mendix integrations.

question: Daily import of 1000 customer rows. 200 already exist by email; 800 are new. Object Handling = Find by key on Email. After import?
explanation: Find by key is upsert. Match → update; no match → insert. 200 existing emails get updated; 800 fresh ones get inserted. Create object always would have inserted 200 duplicates.

question: You publish a REST endpoint with both Anonymous user enabled and Basic auth available. A request arrives without credentials. What context applies?
options: Treated as Anonymous, runs under the Anonymous user role's access rules
explanation: With Anonymous enabled, missing creds fall through to the Anonymous role. The endpoint runs under that role's permissions — so configure those rules tightly. 401 only fires if Anonymous isn't enabled.

question: A Java action opens a JDBC connection to an external database, runs a query, returns. Memory grows over time. Likely cause?
options: The action doesn't close the Connection/ResultSet; use try-with-resources or finally-close
explanation: Classic resource leak — connections and result sets must be closed. try-with-resources is the idiomatic Java fix. Mendix doesn't manage external JDBC connections for you. GC speed isn't the issue.

question: You need a Java action that reads Customer rows even when the calling user lacks Read access. Approach?
options: Refactor the action to take pre-loaded data as parameter
Use the Core API's system/sudo context to retrieve with elevated rights
explanation: Sudo context lets your Java action perform privileged operations explicitly. Use sparingly and audit. Disabling rules globally is dangerous. try/catch suppresses errors but doesn't elevate. Refactoring to take data avoids the issue but isn't always feasible.

question: You add a private helper method inside the generated MyJavaAction.java OUTSIDE the //BEGIN USER CODE markers. What happens on next deploy?
options: Studio Pro preserves it as a sibling method
The helper is overwritten by code generation
Studio Pro warns you about non-marker code
Studio Pro creates a new marker around it
explanation: Code outside USER CODE markers is unconditionally overwritten on regeneration. No warnings, no auto-marker. Put helpers INSIDE the markers or in a separate utility class.

question: You write Java code using proxy classes to read Customer.Email. The domain model is later changed to rename Email → ContactEmail. What happens to your Java code?
options: It compiles successfully but fails at runtime
It fails to compile — proxies regenerate to match the new domain model, removing the old getter
explanation: Type-safe proxy access is a strength: rename surfaces as a compile error, not a silent runtime bug. You then update Java to match. Without proxies (raw XPath strings) the breakage would only show at runtime, harder to find.

question: You need custom code that reads the device's microphone. Java or JavaScript action?
options: JavaScript action — device APIs are accessible only client-side
Neither — Mendix doesn't support hardware APIs
explanation: Microphone, camera, GPS — device hardware lives on the client. JavaScript actions called from nanoflows reach navigator.mediaDevices. Java runs server-side and can't touch client hardware.

knowledgePath: Events > Practical > After Commit Side Effect
question: Your Order's After Commit handler sends a confirmation email via REST. The commit succeeds and the email is sent. Then the calling microflow throws and rolls back. What's the database state?
options: Both the Order commit and the email are rolled back
The Order is rolled back; the email was already sent — external side effects aren't transactional
The After Commit handler is re-triggered
explanation: After Commit fires inside the transaction, but external side effects (emails, REST) bypass transactional semantics. Rollback undoes DB state but not what's already left the system. Defer external work to AFTER the commit completes for guaranteed consistency.

question: Your Before Commit handler on Order conditionally modifies an attribute and calls Commit on Order. What happens?
options: The second Commit is a no-op
Infinite loop: each Commit fires Before Commit, which Commits, which fires Before Commit...
explanation: Before Commit fires on every commit — including ones triggered from inside the handler. Infinite recursion. Mendix does NOT auto-detect this. The fix is to use Change Object inside the handler (no explicit Commit) so the OUTER commit persists the modified state.

question: Person has a Required rule on Email. You create Employee specializing Person. A microflow creates Employee without setting Email and commits. What happens?
options: The commit succeeds — Employee skips Person's rules
The commit fails — validation rules ARE inherited (unlike access rules)
explanation: Validation rules inherit downward. Employee gets all of Person's rules automatically. Confusing this with access rules (NOT inherited) is a common trap. Validation = inherited; Access = explicit per entity.

question: You want 'deletes' on Order to actually mark IsDeleted=true (soft delete). Implementation?
options: Override Delete in the System module
Before Delete handler: set IsDeleted=true on the object, then return false to cancel the physical delete
After Delete handler that re-inserts a tombstone
explanation: Before Delete returning false cancels the actual delete. Set IsDeleted=true and return false. Pair with XPath constraints `[IsDeleted = false()]` everywhere to hide soft-deleted rows. After Delete fires AFTER actual delete — too late.

question: You're bulk-importing 100k rows. Validation rules on each row run on every commit, slowing things massively. Acceptable optimization?
options: Use the 'without events and without validation' commit variant during the import, then run validation as a one-off review afterwards
explanation: Mendix offers a commit variant that skips events and validation — for trusted bulk imports. Validate post-import in a review microflow to catch issues. Removing rules permanently isn't safe; disabling security creates exposure; RAM helps but isn't structural.

question: You have an enum OrderStatus with value 'Open'. After 6 months, you want to rename 'Open' to 'Active'. Safe approach?
options: Add 'Active' as a new value, write a migration microflow updating rows from 'Open' to 'Active', then remove 'Open'
explanation: Names are immutable once data references them. Add new, migrate data, remove old. Captions can be renamed but the Name (stored value) is fixed. Deleting then re-adding loses references.

question: Your app has an API key constant for an external service. You set Exposed to Client = Yes for convenience. Security implication?
options: No issue — Exposed only affects which flows can access it
Major issue — exposed constants ship to the browser; anyone with dev tools can read the API key
No issue — Mendix encrypts exposed constants
No issue — clients can only read constants in admin mode
explanation: Exposed constants are shipped to client devices. Browser dev tools reveal them. NEVER expose secrets — API keys, passwords, tokens — even temporarily. Use Exposed only for non-sensitive feature flags or display preferences.

question: You log `$order/Status/getCaption()` to the server log for diagnostics. After adding Dutch translations, logs become mixed-language. Why? Fix?
options: getCaption() returns the locale-specific text — use getKey() instead for language-independent logs
explanation: getCaption() is locale-sensitive (English for English users, Dutch for Dutch users). For diagnostics use getKey() — always the technical Name, language-independent. Simple fix once you know the distinction.

question: In production you need PartnerApiUrl = 'https://prod.partner.com', in test = 'https://test.partner.com'. Setup?
options: One constant with default = 'https://test.partner.com', override per environment in cloud config to prod URL
Hardcode the URL in the microflow
Use a microflow that picks based on context
explanation: One constant, per-environment override. Cloud env configuration sets the value at deploy time. Two constants doubles management. Hardcoding requires rebuild per environment. Conditional microflow logic reinvents constants.

question: A scheduled event runs every 10 minutes but sometimes takes 15 minutes. Default behavior?
options: The 10-minute slot during the long run is queued and starts immediately after
The 10-minute slot is skipped; the next attempted run is the next nominal 10-minute mark
An error is logged and the event is disabled
explanation: Default = Skip Next. Long runs cause subsequent scheduled fires to be skipped until the current one finishes. After that, the next nominal time fires. Skip Next is conservative; 'Delay Next' is the alternative that queues.

question: A nightly emails-summary scheduled event sends emails to 1000 users. Mendix Cloud restarts halfway through. Best design?
options: Track per-user 'last_summary_sent_date' so retries skip already-emailed users — idempotent
Disable the event until manually resumed
explanation: Scheduled events don't checkpoint mid-run. A restart aborts the in-flight execution; the next fire starts fresh. Without idempotency, half your users get double emails. Track per-user state to detect already-done work.

question: Your app runs on a Mendix Cloud cluster with 3 nodes. A daily scheduled event is configured. How many fires per day across the cluster?
explanation: Mendix's scheduler coordinates across nodes — daily means once globally, not per node. Per-node concurrency limit (10) is separate from how often an event fires. Without cluster awareness, daily cleanup would run 3x and corrupt data.

question: A scheduled event microflow throws an uncaught exception. What happens at the next scheduled time?
options: The error is logged but the next fire happens normally
All scheduled events in the module are paused
explanation: Failures are logged but don't pause future runs. Design scheduled events to be self-healing: catch errors inside, log appropriately, and ensure subsequent runs can recover from previous failures.

knowledgePath: Scheduled Events > Practical > UTC vs Local
question: You want a daily report at 9:00 AM Amsterdam time (CET, UTC+1 in winter, UTC+2 in summer). Best schedule configuration?
options: Daily at 8:00 UTC (Amsterdam winter time) — accept ±1 hour during DST transitions
Schedule via app logic, not the scheduler
explanation: Mendix Cloud runs UTC. Choose UTC time that approximates Amsterdam 9 AM in the dominant season. Winter (UTC+1) → 8:00 UTC. Summer (UTC+2) → 7:00 UTC. Accept ±1 hour shift during DST changes. For true per-user time, fan out hourly and filter.

question: Sprint planning: PO wants 15 story points worth of work. The team's recent velocity is 12. Best response?
options: Commit to 15 to satisfy the PO
Commit to ~12 based on actual velocity; pick the highest-priority items
explanation: Velocity is your honest predictor. Committing more leads to burnout and incomplete work. The PO chooses WHICH items based on priority; the team chooses HOW MUCH based on capacity. Padding for politics breaks trust.

question: A story is estimated at 13 points. What should you do?
options: Split it — large stories carry high risk and usually contain multiple smaller increments of value
Re-estimate as 8 to fit a sprint
explanation: 13 points is a smell. Almost always splittable. Smaller increments reduce risk, ship value sooner, allow course correction. Reassigning doesn't reduce risk. Re-estimating downward is dishonest.

question: Three sprints in a row the retro produces 'merge conflicts on shared microflows' as an action item. What does this signal?
options: The team needs more git training
The action item isn't being addressed — try a structural fix (e.g. split frequently-edited microflows into smaller sub-microflows)
Add coding standards forbidding shared microflows
explanation: Recurring action items mean the structural fix isn't tried. In Mendix specifically, large microflows are merge magnets — split them up. Coding standards alone can't enforce architecture; pausing parallel work kills velocity.

question: For a Mendix project, what should the Definition of Done include?
options: Code reviewed, security access rules verified, deployed to test env, accepted by PO, documented per team standards
explanation: DoD is the team's quality bar. For Mendix specifically, security verification (access rules!) is essential — defaults can drift from policy. Test coverage targets vary by team. Persistability is a design choice, not a DoD criterion.

question: While building an MVP, a team starts implementing a sophisticated user-permissions matrix because 'we'll need it eventually'. Agile critique?
options: Speculative scope delays validation. Defer non-essential complexity until the core hypothesis is validated
It's a PO decision; not a critique
Permissions are foundational; this is correct
explanation: MVP discipline: ship the smallest thing that validates the hypothesis. Sophisticated permissions might be needed in v2 but block v1 learnings. 'We'll need it eventually' is the most expensive sentence in product development.

question: Your team wants to auto-deploy main to production every commit. Safest Mendix pattern?
options: Auto-deploy to staging, run tests, then a manual approval gate to production
Deploy from Studio Pro on Fridays
explanation: Mature CD: auto-deploy to staging, run automated tests, manual approval to prod. Pure commit-to-prod is risky for business apps. Friday deploys are the meme; Mendix supports CD with proper guardrails.

question: A platform supports thousands of tenant orgs. Each tenant has Customers, Products, etc. Best multi-tenant model?
options: All tenants share the same entities; every entity has a Tenant association; access rules constrain by current user's Tenant
Schema-per-tenant in the database, configured manually
explanation: Mendix for Platforms is purpose-built for multi-tenant scenarios. Option B (single-app multi-tenancy via Tenant association + access rules) is the DIY pattern and works for moderate scale, but Mendix for Platforms handles isolation, scaling, billing per tenant — recommended for serious multi-tenancy.

knowledgePath: Domain Model > Practical > Hot Attribute Update
question: Customer.LastSeenAt should update on every user activity. With 100K users daily, you risk row-level contention. Best approach?
options: Update LastSeenAt synchronously on every request
Throttle: track last update per user in memory, write to DB at most every 60 seconds
Drop LastSeenAt — it's not worth the cost
explanation: Hot rows under heavy update cause lock contention. Throttling (write-coalescing) cuts writes 60x with minimal accuracy loss. Synchronous on every request scales poorly. Dropping data is loss of capability. Calculated attributes are read-only and don't solve the problem.

question: You have Events: ClickEvent, PurchaseEvent, ViewEvent. Each has different attributes but you query them together for analytics. Best model?
options: Three unrelated entities and three separate queries
Single Event entity with JSON-blob attribute for type-specific data
Abstract Event generalization with specializations per type
Single Event entity with all possible attributes nullable
explanation: Generalization gives queryable polymorphism: retrieve Event to get all types; retrieve a specific specialization for type-aware logic. Three unrelated entities lose the unified queryability. JSON-blob attributes lose type safety. Wide-nullable schemas waste space and obscure intent.

question: You log sensor readings: 10 sensors × 1 reading/second × 1 year = ~300M rows. Best design?
options: A SensorReading entity with index on (sensor, timestamp)
Offload time-series to a specialized database (InfluxDB, TimescaleDB) accessed via REST/External Entity; keep aggregates in Mendix
One big SensorReading entity; let Mendix optimize
Multiple SensorReading entities, one per sensor
explanation: Mendix's relational backing isn't tuned for time-series. 300M+ rows with complex aggregation crushes traditional RDBMS. Specialized TSDBs handle this elegantly. Mendix integrates via REST or External Entities. Indexed approach helps but won't match a TSDB at scale; multi-entity workarounds explode the model.

question: Regulatory compliance requires you to audit every change to Patient records: who changed what, when, with old/new values, immutable. Approach?
options: Use the changedBy + changedDate system members
After Commit handler that copies the object to a PatientHistory entity with versioning
Use Mendix Cloud's built-in audit log
Java action that diffs and persists to a write-once table
explanation: True audit requires diff capture and write-once semantics. Java actions plus a write-only Audit entity with database-level append-only constraints fit best. System members capture WHO/WHEN but not WHAT changed. After Commit copy works for full snapshots but lacks fine-grained diff. Mendix Cloud audit is for platform events, not data changes.

question: You need to process 100K Orders. Synchronous microflow takes 30+ minutes and times out. Best architectural pattern?
options: Batch into chunks (e.g. 100 orders each) and use Mendix Queues / Task Queue for async processing with retries
explanation: Long-running synchronous work doesn't fit a request-response model. Chunking + a task queue gives observability, retries, parallelism. Mendix Queues (beta) or community queue modules support this. Java threading is fragile and ignores Mendix's runtime model. Recursion still runs in one transaction.

question: Two users edit the same Customer simultaneously. User A saves first. User B tries to save 30 seconds later — overwrites A's changes. How to detect/prevent?
options: Use a Lock entity to serialize access
Use the System.changedDate: include it as a version stamp and reject saves where the stored value is newer
Always show a confirm dialog before save
First-write-wins is acceptable for non-financial data
explanation: Optimistic concurrency: each save includes the version (e.g. changedDate when loaded), server compares with current stored version, rejects stale saves. Lock entities (pessimistic) work but block legitimate concurrent reads. First-write-wins (lost updates) is a real data integrity hazard. Confirm dialogs depend on the user noticing.

question: Your microflow creates a local Order, then calls an external Payment API to charge the customer. Payment succeeds but the Mendix commit fails. Now what?
options: Mendix transactions extend to external systems
No automatic rollback of the payment — you need to either implement a compensation (refund) flow OR ensure the local commit happens BEFORE the payment (with idempotency)
explanation: Distributed transactions are out of Mendix's scope (and impossible in many setups). Choose: (a) commit local first, then payment with idempotency key — if payment fails, you can retry; (b) implement explicit compensation (refund) microflows for failure cases. Naive retries can cause double-charges.

question: A microflow called on every page load takes 200ms, dominated by a 'Retrieve All Configurations' query that returns 50 rows. Best optimization?
options: Cache configuration in app-level constants or a single retrieve at startup; subsequent calls read from memory
Add an index on the Configuration table
explanation: Configurations rarely change but are read constantly. Cache once at startup (or first read) in a singleton-style holder. Constants only work for static values. Indexes help but per-page DB retrieval is still wasteful. Async doesn't help if downstream depends on the result.

question: A 'request approval' process involves: user submits → manager reviews (may take days) → approves/denies → notifications. Right tool?
options: Mendix Workflow (WDK) — designed for durable, multi-step, multi-actor processes
A series of pages with conditional navigation
explanation: Workflow Devkit (WDK) is purpose-built for durable, pausable processes spanning days/weeks with multiple actors. Microflows are stateless per-request. Polling is brittle. Page-conditional navigation lacks audit, retries, and timer-based escalation.

question: Two field workers edit the same Customer offline. Both reconnect and Synchronize. What does Mendix do?
options: First write succeeds; the second commit is rejected as a sync conflict; the app must handle the conflict UX
Both writes succeed; Mendix logs a warning
explanation: Default optimistic concurrency: second sync hits a version mismatch and is rejected. The app must catch this and present a conflict-resolution UX. Last-write-wins requires opt-in. Field-level merging is not built in. Treating sync as magic causes silent data loss.

question: In a nanoflow you loop 100 iterations, calling Show Progress Bar each iteration. The UI doesn't visibly update. Why?
options: Show Progress Bar requires a microflow
JS runs synchronously by default; the loop completes in one tick without yielding to the renderer. Insert an async pause (Promise-returning JS action) inside the loop to yield
explanation: Synchronous JS doesn't repaint until it yields. The loop runs in one tick, then the final state shows. Adding `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 0))` between iterations gives the browser a chance to repaint. This is general JS behavior — surfaces in nanoflows because they run as JS.

question: Your offline mobile app needs to silently sync data while in background. Approach?
options: A regular nanoflow with a setInterval
A JavaScript action that registers a Service Worker (PWA) handling background sync events
Just use synchronize on app open
explanation: Background sync requires platform-level capability (Service Workers in web, background tasks on mobile). Nanoflows can register them via JS actions. setInterval works only while the app is in foreground. Scheduled events run server-side, irrelevant to client background work.

question: On a form, a nanoflow validates the email format AND a microflow checks if it's already taken in the database. Both run on field-blur. Race condition possible?
options: Yes — the microflow's async result might arrive after the user has moved to the next field; design with proper async sequencing or debouncing
explanation: Async validation has classic race risks: by the time the server responds, the UI may have moved on. Debounce input, cancel pending checks on new input, and clearly indicate the field's validation state. Mendix doesn't auto-serialize concurrent async work.

question: An offline app processes large lists of NPEs without committing. Over time, the device runs out of memory. Why?
options: NPEs persist as long as anything references them; long-lived references (e.g. on the session or global state) prevent GC. Explicitly null out references when done
JavaScript GC is disabled in nanoflows
explanation: GC reclaims unreferenced objects. If your code holds NPEs in a session-scoped variable, they live forever. Audit references, clear lists after use, use scoped variables. Mendix doesn't impose arbitrary memory limits; GC is normal JavaScript behavior.

question: Module A depends on B. New requirement needs A's microflow used by B too. Solution?
options: Refactor: extract the shared microflow to a third Module C; both A and B depend on C
Use a published REST service within the same app
explanation: Mendix forbids circular dependencies, and circular dependencies are an architecture smell anyway. Extract to a shared module C with no app-specific opinions. REST-within-app is a hack with real overhead. Inline-copying breaks DRY and lets two implementations drift.

knowledgePath: Modules > Practical > Renaming a Public API
question: You ship an add-on module v1.5 with entity Customer. v2 renames it to Account. Consumer apps reference Customer in pages and microflows. Best release strategy?
options: Just rename — consumers can use Find & Replace
Provide v2 as a major version bump with migration guide; document the breaking change clearly; consider keeping Customer as a deprecated alias for one minor version
Don't rename; keep both Customer and Account forever
Rename and force everyone to upgrade simultaneously
explanation: Public APIs deserve respect for downstream impact. Major version bump signals breaking change; migration guides reduce friction; transitional aliases (when feasible) ease upgrades. Forcing immediate upgrade or living with two names indefinitely both have costs.

question: You use Marketplace add-on Encryption module. Its encrypt() microflow uses AES-128. You need AES-256 for compliance. The module is .mxmodule (protected). How to customize?
options: Override in your own module: wrap the add-on's encrypt() in your own microflow that calls AES-256 via a Java action
Ask Mendix to ship a v2
explanation: Protected modules can't be edited. The pattern is to compose around them: your own wrapping microflow calling a Java action for AES-256, bypassing the add-on for the specific use case. Decompilation isn't supported; waiting for upstream is too slow.

question: You're an ISV shipping a 'CRM Solution' as a Solution module to multiple customers, each with custom needs. Architectural concern?
options: Solution modules don't support customization — sell App modules instead
Design extension points: declare microflows as Usable so customers can override them; use specializations as customization mechanism; consider configuration entities customers set per deploy
Allow customers to fork your module
Lock everything to prevent customer changes
explanation: Successful Solution modules predict customization needs. Public-facing microflows at Usable export level let customers override; specializations extend entities; configuration entities parameterize behavior. Forking destroys upgrade paths; locking everything limits adoption.

question: Your CRM module now has 50 entities, 200 microflows, 30 pages. Compilation is slow, navigation is hard. Strategic response?
options: Live with it — modularization isn't worth the effort
Split into 3-5 focused modules: e.g. CRM_Domain (entities), CRM_API (REST services), CRM_UI (pages), CRM_Workflow (orchestration). Compile time improves and maintainability skyrockets
explanation: Mendix modules have a sweet spot in size. Bloat slows compile, hurts navigability, hides architectural intent. Split by concern. Hardware doesn't fix structural issues. System module is for built-ins, off-limits.

question: Your published REST API authenticates via JWT in Authorization header. Implementation in Mendix?
options: Basic & Active Session with custom logic
Anonymous access plus JWT validation inside each microflow
Custom Microflow authentication: Mendix passes the request to your microflow, you parse and verify JWT, return a System.User
OAuth — Mendix has built-in JWT validation
explanation: Custom Microflow auth is the path for token-based schemes. Mendix doesn't ship a built-in JWT validator (community modules exist). Anonymous + in-microflow checks bypass the published auth contract. Basic auth doesn't parse JWTs.

question: You store credit card numbers temporarily for retry purposes. Compliance requires encryption at rest, AND access to clear-text only via specific microflows. Approach?
options: Encrypt the attribute using a Java action on Before Commit; decrypt only inside authorized microflows; pair with strict access rules so the encrypted attribute is never displayed raw
explanation: Encryption-at-rest requires explicit logic. Encrypt on commit, decrypt only when needed via authorized microflows. Access rules hide the encrypted blob. Transport encryption protects data in motion, not at rest. Hashed string is one-way (can't decrypt). Mendix Cloud encrypts the database but app-level access still sees clear values.

question: You log security-sensitive events to an Audit entity. You discover Audit rows are sometimes missing when the original microflow fails. Why?
options: The Audit insert is rolled back along with the failing transaction — wrap Audit logging in a 'Custom without rollback' error handler, or commit Audit BEFORE the main transaction
Database constraints reject duplicate audit rows
explanation: Transactions are atomic — if the main operation rolls back, so does the Audit insert (because it's in the same transaction). For tamper-evident audit, commit Audit FIRST (or use a separate service that doesn't participate in the main transaction). 'Custom without rollback' preserves the Audit creation across failures.

question: A REST endpoint accepts Customer data. A malicious client POSTs extra fields like `isAdmin: true`. Mass assignment bypass?
options: Mendix's mapping ignores unmapped fields automatically
Define an explicit Import Mapping that lists only allowed attributes; extra fields in JSON are ignored. Never use 'Map all attributes' for security-sensitive entities
explanation: Explicit attribute mapping is your whitelist. Mendix Import Mappings only set attributes you've mapped — extra JSON fields are dropped. 'Map all attributes' is dangerous because new attributes added later are auto-included. HTTPS protects transport but doesn't prevent mass assignment.

question: User Role 'Manager' includes Module Role A_Editor and Module Role B_Viewer. Both rules apply to Shared.Item — A_Editor allows Write, B_Viewer is Read-only. Effective access?
options: Read+Write — access rules are additive across module roles
explanation: Access rules combine via UNION across module roles in a user role. Manager gets Write because A_Editor allows it. To restrict, narrow A_Editor's rule itself. This OPPOSITE-of-Unix-permissions behavior trips up many access designers.

question: You display a list of 10K rows that all need to be visible at once (no paging). Performance is terrible. Strategic fix?
options: Use Data Grid 2 or a List View with virtualization — only visible rows render to DOM
Render to an external HTML widget
explanation: DOM with 10K rows kills any browser. Virtualization renders only visible rows + buffer. Data Grid 2 supports it. Classic Data Grid does not. Pagination changes UX. External widgets work but lose Mendix's integration.

question: A page has 200 Conditional Visibility expressions. Typing feels sluggish. Why?
options: Each keystroke triggers re-evaluation of all 200 expressions client-side. Group fields under shared conditional containers, simplify expressions, or move logic to computed attributes
explanation: Conditional expressions run on every state change. 200 expressions × every keystroke = perceptible lag. Structural fix: fewer, broader conditionals; precomputed attributes for complex logic; container-level conditionals over field-level.

question: A heavy admin page has 5 tabs, each with its own data view and microflow data source. Page load is slow because all 5 microflows fire on render. Optimization?
options: Use 'Lazy load' on the tabs so each microflow fires only when its tab is activated
explanation: Lazy loading tabs defers microflow execution until needed. 5 separate flows running upfront wastes time on tabs the user might not visit. Combining microflows compounds the latency. Native mobile is irrelevant. Caching helps but lazy load is the structural fix.

question: You have a complex 'OrderSummary' snippet used on 10 different pages. Each page has different surrounding actions. How do you keep the snippet generic?
options: Pass an Action object (microflow reference) as a snippet parameter — each page configures its own behavior
Hardcode all 10 actions inside the snippet with conditional visibility
Don't reuse — copy the snippet per page
explanation: Snippets can receive object parameters; microflow references via parameters let callers inject behavior. 10 variants violates DRY. Conditional visibility for 10 actions is brittle. Copy-paste defeats the purpose of snippets.

question: You need a Gantt chart in your app. No Mendix-native widget. Approach?
options: Build a Mendix Pluggable Widget using React; render a Gantt library (e.g. dhtmlx-gantt); expose props for data and event handlers
explanation: Pluggable Widgets are the proper extension mechanism for custom UI. React-based, well-documented, integrate with Mendix's data flow. Show Page hacks don't render charts; PDFs aren't interactive; standard widgets can't replicate complex visualizations.

question: You want Customers who have at least one Order whose Total > 1000 in the last 30 days. Single XPath?
explanation: XPath supports compound predicates inside association paths. The single query is efficient — translated to a JOIN with WHERE at the database level. Multiple queries lose this optimization; Java SQL bypasses Mendix abstractions; loops are O(N) on the client.

question: `//Vehicle.Vehicle` returns Cars and Trucks too. You want ONLY base Vehicles (not specializations). How?
options: [not(Car) and not(Truck)] — but only works if you know all specializations and they're directly nested
Retrieve all then filter in microflow via Object Type Decision
XPath has no built-in type filter; refactor your model to use an enum 'Kind' on Vehicle instead of inheritance
explanation: Mendix XPath doesn't expose a type filter. The pragmatic approach is to retrieve all Vehicles then drop specializations via Object Type Decision. Option D (refactor) is heavier but sometimes the right call. Option B works only with explicit enumeration.

question: Inside a microflow that processes a List of Orders, you want to constrain a Retrieve so the result excludes the current Order being processed. XPath?
options: XPath doesn't support self-exclusion; filter post-retrieve
explanation: Direct entity comparison: `[Sales.Order != $currentOrder]` excludes the specific row. Comparing by id requires accessing the system id; not always exposed. The `.` self-reference isn't standard. Post-filtering is wasteful.

question: Find Projects where the assigned Manager has more than 5 direct reports. Manager has association `DirectReports` to Employee.
options: Both A and C are equivalent (count usable in Java contexts)
explanation: Both forms express the same idea. Inside Java/service XPath, count() can be used in predicates. Inside Studio Pro, aggregate functions are limited so workarounds may be needed. Option B compares the association reference to 5, syntactically wrong.

question: You have an access rule with a 4-hop XPath. The table is 10M rows. Adding the appropriate composite indexes improved things to 200ms per query, but you need sub-50ms. Architectural next step?
options: Denormalize: maintain a direct attribute that captures the result of the 4-hop join, updated by event handlers
explanation: Denormalization trades write cost (event handlers maintain the direct attribute) for blazing-fast reads. At sub-50ms targets on big tables, joins inherently cost too much. Indexes help but plateau. Caching has invalidation issues. Archiving reduces scope but doesn't solve query design.

question: App A publishes an event when an Order is placed. App B subscribes and creates a corresponding shipment record. The network is unreliable. Architectural pattern for guaranteed delivery?
options: Synchronous REST call from A to B
Mendix Business Events on a durable queue with at-least-once delivery; B's subscriber is idempotent
Polling: B polls A every minute
explanation: Business Events on a durable queue persist events on the producer side; the broker retries delivery to subscribers. Subscribers must be idempotent because at-least-once means duplicates are possible. Synchronous REST couples reliability across services. Polling has freshness issues. Email is not an integration mechanism.

question: A purchase workflow needs to: (1) reserve inventory, (2) charge payment, (3) create shipping label, (4) confirm to user. Each can fail. Best pattern?
options: A single microflow with all 4 calls and rollback on any failure
Saga: each step is a separate transaction with a corresponding compensation step (release inventory, refund, etc.); orchestrate via Workflow Devkit
explanation: Saga is the gold-standard for distributed transactions across systems that can't share a transaction boundary. Each step has a compensation. WDK orchestrates the saga with durability. Single-microflow rollback only works for local DB state — external calls don't roll back. XA transactions aren't supported across heterogeneous systems.

question: A partner API allows 100 requests per minute. Your app needs to call it 10K times to process a backlog. Approach?
